question.text: One mole of a monoatomic real gas satisfies the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>RT</mi></math> where b is a constant. The relationship of interatomic potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and interatomic distance r for the gas is given by

solution.text:
Here the given equation is P(V-b)=RT.
On comparing with van der Waals' equation
P+aV2[V-b]=RT
That is a=0.
It means only repulsive forces are present which are contributive only at very close distance so the potential energy will increase abruptly. i.e., graph C is correct.
